questions.question: What does Rob do before he goes to work at the fire station?
questions.explanation: This question checks if children remember that Rob says goodbye to his family and gets ready for work, connecting his caring attitude to his important job.

questions.question: Why do Rob and his friends check their equipment at the fire station?
questions.explanation: This question helps children see how preparation and teamwork keep everyone safe, showing how firefighters work together.

questions.question: Can you remember a time when you helped a friend or worked together with others? What did you do?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to connect the story's teamwork to their own lives, building empathy and the habit of helping others.

questions.question: What did the firefighters do when the second-grade class visited? Why do you think they did that?
questions.explanation: Helps children see how firefighters care for others by teaching them to be safe.

questions.question: How did Rob help Michelle's dog, Pickles? How do you think Michelle felt when her dog was safe?
questions.explanation: Allows children to imagine the feelings of others, understanding kindness and bravery in helping.

questions.question: What did the other firefighters do while Rob helped Pickles? How did everyone work together?
questions.explanation: Shows how helping and teamwork keep people and pets safe, reinforcing that everyone has an important job.

questions.question: If you saw someone who needed help, what could you do?
questions.explanation: Applies the story's lesson to real life, encouraging children to think about helping others in ways they can.

questions.question: Why do you think Rob smiled at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: Prompts children to think about the happiness we feel after helping others, reinforcing the story’s moral.

questions.question: What are some ways you can be safe, like the children in Ms. Hill’s class learned?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to remember fire safety and think of their own actions, making the lesson personal.

questions.question: Rob had many jobs at the fire station. Why is it important for everyone to help with different jobs?
questions.explanation: Helps children understand the value of teamwork and doing our part, connecting to the story’s lesson about working together.

moral: Firefighters work hard to help people and keep everyone safe. They do many important jobs, and they care about others. Working together and helping people makes a difference.
learning_objectives: Children will understand how firefighters help people and keep everyone safe.
Children will recognize examples of teamwork and caring for others.
Children will reflect on ways they can help others and work together in their own lives.
Children will discuss basic fire safety rules and why they matter.
